newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-ALANIA HAND CHAMPIONS SPARTAK WORST DEFEAT OF YEAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALANIA HAND CHAMPIONS SPARTAK WORST DEFEAT OF YEAR.

text.p: Spartak Moscow, capital rivals Dynamo and Rotor Volgograd share the lead in the Russian premier league after both Spartak and Rotor suffered costly defeats on Wednesday. Dynamo managed only a draw at home.
Last year's runners-up Alania Vladikavkaz gave their best display of a disappointing season to hand champions Spartak a 2-0 defeat, their worst result of the year.
The 1995 champions, meeting Spartak for the first time since losing the championship playoff last November, dominated much of the game.
They scored through Sergei Timofeyev's long-range shot in the 28th minute and Levan Kobiashvili's solo strike 11 minutes later.
The scoreline did not reflect the total dominance by the home team as Alania wasted numerous chances in the second half.

The Muscovites woke up only in the last 10 minutes when first Andrei Tikhonov headed the ball straight at Vladikavkaz goalkeeper Dmitry Kramarenko and then second-half substitute Maxim Buznikin missed with the goal gaping at his mercy.
It was a crucial win for Alania, who prior to this match trailed top-of-the-table Spartak by 11 points.
Joint leaders Rotor failed to take advantage of Spartak's slip, losing 2-1 at home to fourth-placed Torpedo LM Moscow.
Dynamo, who started the day one point behind the leaders, were held to a scoreless draw at home by Chernomorets Novorossiisk.
Another of Moscow's big five teams, CSKA, dropped into the unfamiliar territory of the relegation zone.
Now third from bottom, the army team are in real danger of going down after suffering their second successive defeat, 3-1 to Lokomotiv in Nizhny Novgorod.
CSKA, once a powerhouse of Soviet soccer and the last team to win the now defunct Soviet league in 1991, suffered a wholesale close-season defection to Torpedo after a row over the club's ownership.
